Seminar Title:

Development of a Sequential Deep Learning Framework for Vibration-Based Structural Damage Identification and Optimal Sensor Placement for Bridges

Seminar Type:

Synopsis Seminar

Department:

Civil Engineering

Speaker Name:

Tanmay Das ( Rollno : 521ce1014)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

Seminar Room, Department of Civil Engineering

Date and Time:

09 Oct 2026 10.00 AM

Contact:

Shyamal Guchhait

Abstract:

The present research explores the use of deep learning for bridge damage identification directly from raw time-domain acceleration responses, avoiding the explicit extraction of modal parameters or other hand-crafted damage-sensitive features. The work progressively addresses damage localisation, severity estimation, multiple-damage identification, and sensor optimisation, with particular emphasis on bridge structural health monitoring. Initially, the feasibility of direct damage identification is investigated using a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (2D CNN), followed by a comparative evaluation of various deep learning architectures. The study subsequently develops hybrid long short-term memory (LSTM) and gated recurrent unit (GRU) models to improve damage identification, particularly in the presence of measurement noise. The methodology is further advanced through a hierarchical dual-stage framework, where damage localisation is followed by severity assessment using multiclass classification algorithms in both stages. This concept is subsequently extended by formulating a sequential DL algorithm in which localisation is treated as a classification problem and severity estimation as a continuous regression problem. The framework is also applied to previously unseen multiple damage combinations using models trained only on individual-damage scenarios, enabling sequential identification without requiring every possible damage combination during training. Physical response sensitivity and latent-feature distance are examined to interpret the resulting identification order. Finally, a hybrid unsupervised sensor-optimisation framework combining proper orthogonal decomposition (POD) with QR pivoting and a self-attention autoencoder with integrated gradient (SAAE-IG) through Entropy-Weighted Grey Relational Analysis (EW-GRA) is developed to reduce sensing requirements while retaining damage-identification performance. Numerical investigations, together with experimental data from the Z24, Old ADA, S101, and HBTA bridge datasets, demonstrate the applicability of the developed approaches to vibration based bridge structural health monitoring.
